name: Contour bunding with farm pond
tradeoffs: Removes 3-5% of cultivable area for bunds and pond footprint
Mosquito breeding risk if pond water stagnates without fish or flow
mechanism: Contour bunds intercept overland runoff and route it to a farm pond, extending the infiltration window, raising the shallow water table and creating perennial microhabitat.

name: Legume cover cropping between main-crop seasons

effects.delta: moderate increase via added floral resources

tradeoffs: Seed and inoculant cost in the off-season with no direct cash return
Requires timely termination before main crop sowing or it competes for moisture
mechanism: Legume cover crops fix atmospheric nitrogen and add root and shoot biomass to the soil between cash-crop cycles, directly raising organic carbon inputs.

sources.title: Soil Organic Carbon: the Hidden Potential

name: Agroforestry boundary and scattered-tree planting

effects.delta: +20-40% species count relative to treeless fields
-3 to -6 C at soil surface under canopy

tradeoffs: Tree roots and shade reduce yield of adjacent crop rows by 5-10%
8-10 year lag before full canopy and timber/fruit returns materialise
mechanism: Boundary and scattered trees add vertical structure and shade, lowering surface temperature and slowing organic matter mineralisation while creating nesting and foraging habitat.

sources.title: Agroforestry and Biodiversity Conservation in Tropical Landscapes

name: Hedgerow and field margin restoration

effects.delta: new corridor habitat along field edges
measurable increase in plant and insect species pool

tradeoffs: Loses 1-3% of field area to non-cropped margin strips
Needs periodic management or it can host crop pests as well as their enemies
mechanism: Semi-natural, undisturbed margins act as movement corridors between habitat patches and provide overwintering refuge for predatory and pollinating insects.

name: No-till / minimum-till conservation agriculture

effects.delta: +0.1-0.2% absolute over 5 years in the top 15cm
-30-50% surface soil loss versus conventional tillage

tradeoffs: Requires specialised no-till seeding equipment, a capital cost barrier
Early transition years can see higher weed pressure and herbicide reliance
mechanism: Leaving residue on the surface and avoiding inversion tillage protects topsoil from raindrop impact and slows the oxidation of soil organic matter.

name: Rotational grazing with rest periods

effects.delta: increased sward height variation across paddocks

tradeoffs: Needs fencing and water-point investment to subdivide paddocks
Requires active herd-movement labour or automation
mechanism: Resting paddocks between grazing bouts lets vegetation recover root reserves and canopy height before re-grazing, building root biomass and surface litter.

name: Vermicompost / farmyard manure amendment
tradeoffs: Bulky input with real transport and labour cost at scale
Nutrient content is variable batch to batch unless tested
mechanism: Composted organic matter is added directly to soil, raising organic carbon and microbial activity faster than in-situ residue decomposition alone.

name: Crop residue mulching
tradeoffs: Residue has competing uses as fodder in mixed crop-livestock systems
Can harbour stem-borer pests if not managed between seasons
mechanism: A surface residue layer blocks direct solar radiation and reduces evaporative loss from the topsoil, buffering both moisture and temperature swings.

name: Check dams for watershed treatment

effects.delta: measurable rise in nearby open-well water levels within one monsoon
-20-40% sediment load in the treated micro-watershed

tradeoffs: Upstream sediment trapping means downstream fields receive less silt renewal
Requires periodic desilting maintenance or storage capacity declines
mechanism: Small check structures across seasonal drainage lines slow flow velocity, letting suspended sediment settle and giving water more time to infiltrate.

name: Native species afforestation of degraded land

effects.delta: substantial increase as native fauna recolonise
-40-60% once canopy and litter layer establish

tradeoffs: 5-7 years of near-zero productive return while trees establish
Wrong species choice (exotic monoculture) can suppress understory biodiversity instead of restoring it
mechanism: Restoring native tree cover rebuilds vertical habitat structure, litter inputs and root systems that stabilise soil, reversing the degradation pathway that removed them.

sources.title: Forest Landscape Restoration and Biodiversity Outcomes

name: Cereal-legume intercropping
tradeoffs: More complex planting, harvest and machinery logistics than monoculture
Requires matching maturity windows of the intercropped species
mechanism: Growing two crops with staggered flowering and rooting patterns extends floral resource availability and spreads climate risk across species.

name: Farm wetland / seasonal pond restoration
tradeoffs: Takes farmland out of production for the wetland footprint
Can increase human-wildlife conflict risk (e.g. waterbirds on adjacent crops)
mechanism: Re-wetting a seasonal depression restores breeding habitat for amphibians and a water source that anchors a wider wetland-associated food web.

name: Beetle banks / raised vegetated refugia
tradeoffs: Small but real loss of cropped area for the raised bank
Benefit is localised near the bank unless spaced through large fields
mechanism: A raised, tussocky grass strip through a field gives ground beetles and spiders a dry overwintering refuge close to the crop they later help protect.

name: Silvopasture (integrating trees into grazing land)

effects.delta: added woody layer over the existing grass layer

tradeoffs: Reduces grazeable area by 10-20% under tree canopy
Requires temporary fencing to protect saplings from livestock
mechanism: Introducing scattered or alley-planted trees into grazing land adds a structural layer above the grass sward, providing shade and diversifying habitat.

sources.title: Agroforestry and Biodiversity Conservation in Tropical Landscapes

name: Drip irrigation conversion

effects.delta: 30-50% less water applied for comparable yield

tradeoffs: High upfront capital cost for pipes, emitters and filtration
Emitters need regular maintenance to prevent clogging in hard water
mechanism: Delivering water directly to the root zone at low flow rates cuts evaporative and runoff losses that flood or furrow irrigation incurs.

name: Windbreak / shelterbelt planting

effects.delta: -15-30% wind-driven topsoil loss in the sheltered zone

tradeoffs: Shades and competes with crops within roughly one tree-height of the belt
Takes 3-5 years to reach effective wind-reduction height
mechanism: A planted tree line reduces wind speed for a distance of several times its height downwind, cutting wind erosion and moisture loss from exposed soil.

sources.title: Forest Landscape Restoration and Biodiversity Outcomes

name: Biochar soil amendment
tradeoffs: Production requires a pyrolysis unit and a feedstock supply chain
Benefits are highly feedstock- and soil-type dependent, variable across sites
mechanism: Pyrolysed organic material is chemically stable in soil for long periods and its porous structure directly increases water and nutrient retention.

name: Riparian buffer strip restoration

effects.delta: new continuous corridor along the watercourse

tradeoffs: Removes cropped or grazed land within the buffer width from production
Needs fencing to exclude livestock from the watercourse itself
mechanism: A vegetated strip along a watercourse filters sediment and nutrients from runoff before it reaches the water, while providing continuous corridor habitat.
